funding_name: CEPF Mediterranean Basin Biodiversity Conservation
funding_focus: Freshwater biodiversity conservation in Mediterranean Basin (water catchment management)
org_type: Non-governmental organizations, community groups, universities, and private enterprises in the Mediterranean Basin
Application Process: Submit Letter of Inquiry (LOI) via CEPF website
past_recipients: Not specified (CEPF has funded many local NGOs in hotspot regions)
geographic_focus: Mediterranean Basin (Southern Europe, North Africa, Middle East)
gotchas: LOI required; must align with Mediterranean Basin ecosystem profile; proposals accepted in English, French, or Arabic
additional_notes: CEPF is a global partnership fund supporting biodiversity hotspots

funding_name: The Iris Prize (The Iris Project) – Youth Nature Conservation Grants
funding_focus: Youth-led projects to protect and restore nature (new ideas, existing or established projects)
org_type: Individuals, teams or organizations worldwide; youth ages 14–24 (different grant categories for different age groups)
Application Process: Online application form on The Iris Project website
past_recipients: N/A (Program is relatively new; past winners are young conservation leaders)
gotchas: Applicants must be within specified youth age ranges for each award category
additional_notes: Three grants awarded annually: $5k (ages 14–24 new idea), $10k (ages 16–24 existing project), $15k (ages 16–24 established project)

funding_name: Pulitzer Center Impact Seed Fund (ISF)
funding_focus: Educational activities on tropical forests, ocean, and climate issues (to enrich student and educator knowledge)
org_type: Professors or researchers at higher education institutions, or student groups led by a professor; project must not be based in Brazil
Application Process: Apply via Pulitzer Center Submittable portal
past_recipients: Not applicable (new micro-grant program)
gotchas: Project activities should engage university students/educators; Brazil projects are excluded
additional_notes: Micro-grants aimed at university community education on environmental impacts

funding_name: Comedy Wildlife Photography Awards
funding_amount: No cash award (prizes in kind – e.g. trophy, safari tours, camera gear)
funding_focus: Wildlife conservation awareness through humorous wildlife photography
org_type: Open to photographers worldwide (amateur or professional)
Application Process: Submit photos via contest website
past_recipients: Past winners include wildlife photographers whose images went viral (e.g., 2021 winner of a laughing seal photo)
gotchas: No monetary grant; winners receive recognition and sponsor prizes
additional_notes: Aims to highlight wildlife conservation messages with humor; founded by professional photographers

funding_name: People’s Trust for Endangered Species – Conservation Insight Grants
funding_focus: Research or field work that aids the conservation of endangered species (except birds)
org_type: Applicants must already be working and established in eligible countries (UK, UK Overseas Territories, or any country NOT classified as high-income by World Bank)
Application Process: Initial short application; selected applicants are invited to submit full proposal
past_recipients: Example recipients: projects on Iberian lynx, Philippine pangolin conservation (various researchers in developing countries)
geographic_focus: Worldwide (excluding high-income countries; UK applicants acceptable)
gotchas: Bird species projects are NOT funded; applicants must be based in eligible (usually developing) countries
additional_notes: Focus on generating scientific evidence to facilitate species conservation; historically known as PTES Worldwide Small Grants

funding_name: Erik Hosking Trust – Awards for Projects on Birds & Natural History (Writing/Art)
funding_focus: Projects of scientific or conservation value on birds or natural history, communicated through writing, photography, art or illustration
org_type: Open to individuals worldwide with projects in ornithology or natural history (especially early-career naturalists)
Application Process: Submit application as described on trust website (written proposal of project)
past_recipients: Past awards often to young wildlife photographers or authors documenting bird life
gotchas: Must be related to ornithology/natural history and use an artistic or literary medium
additional_notes: Named after wildlife photographer Erik Hosking; encourages creative communication of conservation

funding_name: Association of Field Ornithologists – Latin American Membership Program
funding_amount: One-year AFO membership (access to journal, resources; no direct cash)
funding_focus: Capacity building for ornithologists in Latin America via professional society membership
org_type: Individuals based in Latin America or the Caribbean (Mexico, Central/South America, Caribbean) involved in ornithology
Application Process: Submit membership award application (available in English and Spanish)
past_recipients: N/A (multiple individual recipients each year gain membership)
gotchas: Only provides society membership (no funding); aims to connect Latin American ornithologists to global community
additional_notes: Members get access to AFO journal and networking opportunities for one year

funding_name: International Land Coalition – African Environmental Defenders Emergency Fund
funding_amount: Covers emergency needs (relocation, legal aid, medical support) – amounts vary case by case
application_deadline: Rolling (applications accepted any time; decisions within ~48 hours)
funding_focus: Emergency assistance for land and environmental rights defenders in Africa (e.g., threats, injury, legal issues)
org_type: Must be ILC members (individuals in member NGOs or the member organizations themselves); ILC members can apply on behalf of others in need
Application Process: Submit emergency request via online form or email; rapid response within 48 hours
past_recipients: Not publicized due to sensitivity; examples include support for community leaders facing threats in DR Congo or Kenya
geographic_focus: Africa (any country in Africa where ILC has members)
gotchas: Only ILC member organizations/individuals eligible; funds for urgent situations (not standard project grants)
additional_notes: Supports temporary relocation, legal fees, family support, etc., to protect at-risk conservation and land defenders

funding_name: Earth Journalism Network – Story Grants on Marine Issues (Adriatic Sea)
funding_focus: Journalism production on marine environmental issues in the Adriatic Sea (Western Balkans focus)
org_type: Journalists in Western Balkan countries bordering the Adriatic (Croatia, Slovenia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania; also inland Balkans if story ties to Adriatic)
Application Process: Apply via EJN website (online application form)
past_recipients: N/A (story grant recipients are usually individual journalists; past similar EJN grants have funded journalists in the region reporting on marine pollution)
gotchas: Stories must relate to Adriatic marine issues; grant covers reporting costs, not salary
additional_notes: Provides editorial mentorship 1:1 along with funding

funding_name: Brower Youth Awards for Environmental Leadership
grant_funder: Earth Island Institute – New Leaders Initiative
funding_amount: US$3,000 cash prize + week-long trip to San Francisco Bay Area (incl. lodging)
funding_focus: Recognizing outstanding youth environmental change leaders (projects in any environmental topic)
org_type: Youth ages 13–22 in North America (U.S., Canada, Mexico, and select Caribbean islands)
Application Process: Online application via Brower Youth Awards website (nominations/apply directly)
past_recipients: Examples: 2023 winners included youth working on urban agriculture in Detroit, plastics reduction in California, etc.
gotchas: Must be ages 13-22; winners must attend awards week in California (travel provided)
additional_notes: Includes professionally produced short film about each winner’s work

funding_name: EJN Bay of Bengal Climate Communications Grants
funding_amount: Up to INR 90,000 or BDT 125,000 (~US$1,100–$1,200) per grantee
funding_focus: In-depth reporting on climate change impacts in Bay of Bengal coastal regions (India & Bangladesh)
org_type: Early-career or experienced communicators reporting from coastal Bangladesh or coastal India (Bay of Bengal)
Application Process: Apply via EJN site; includes providing a story proposal and work samples
past_recipients: N/A (new program; EJN previously funded similar climate stories in South Asia)
geographic_focus: South Asia (coastal areas of Bangladesh and India)
gotchas: Focus on under-reported climate impacts; provides editorial mentorship along with funds
additional_notes: Priority to local journalists; output expected in local media

funding_name: EJN Biodiversity Media Grants 2025
funding_focus: Building capacity of media organizations to cover conservation and biodiversity issues (especially in high-biodiversity regions)
org_type: Journalism networks, media organizations, journalism schools, or NGOs focused on media training; preference to Global South organizations
Application Process: Online proposal submission via earthjournalism.net
past_recipients: e.g., Past recipients include media NGOs in Indonesia and East Africa building environmental journalism programs
gotchas: Projects can be led by NGOs if focused on training journalists; must strengthen environmental reporting capacity
additional_notes: Funding supports workshops, training, network development for environmental journalism

funding_name: IUCN NL – Land Acquisition Fund for Conservation
funding_focus: Purchase and protection of threatened wildlife habitats and ecosystems (forests, wetlands, etc.)
org_type: Local non-profit conservation organizations (NGOs/CSOs) in Asia, Pacific, Africa, Latin America
Application Process: Submit proposal to IUCN NL per guidelines on website
past_recipients: Examples: Land purchase to expand a reserve in Ecuador; forest protection by a local NGO in Borneo
gotchas: Local (in-country) NGO must be applicant; must demonstrate long-term management of purchased land
additional_notes: Focus on critical habitats; part of IUCN NL small grants for private reserve creation

funding_name: HMANA – Hawk Migration Research Awards
grant_funder: Hawk Migration Association of North America (HMANA)
funding_focus: Field studies on raptor migration ecology, behavior, population monitoring, or conservation
org_type: Researchers (individuals) conducting raptor migration studies; open worldwide (no geographic restriction in text)
Application Process: Submit research proposal by email or form to HMANA
past_recipients: Past recipients include graduate students studying hawk migration corridors in North America and Africa
geographic_focus: Worldwide (projects can be anywhere, historically many in Americas)
gotchas: Must be focused on migratory raptors; only ~2 projects funded per year
additional_notes: Encourages work on connectivity between breeding and wintering grounds of raptors

funding_name: Global EbA Fund (Ecosystem-based Adaptation)
application_deadline: No deadline (applications accepted year-round; biannual funding decisions)
funding_focus: Innovative approaches to ecosystem-based adaptation (climate resilience via natural solutions)
org_type: Non-profit organizations worldwide (projects can be global, regional, or country-specific)
Application Process: Apply online via Global EbA Fund site (continuous intake)
past_recipients: In 2022, funded projects like mangrove restoration in Vietnam, climate-resilient agriculture in Kenya
geographic_focus: Global (any country; no specific country focus)
gotchas: Projects should serve climate-vulnerable communities/ecosystems; 36-month max project length
additional_notes: Jointly managed by IUCN & UNEP; aims to scale up EbA innovations

funding_name: African Biodiversity Fellowship (Oxford/Leventis)
grant_funder: University of Oxford – A.G. Leventis Foundation
funding_amount: Fully-funded 2–3 month research visit at Oxford (incl. travel, stipend provided)
application_deadline: No fixed deadline (calls are periodic; currently open)
funding_focus: Capacity-building for conservation practitioners in Africa (academic training, networking at Oxford University)
org_type: Early to mid-career biodiversity conservation professionals in NGO, government or business in Africa
Application Process: Apply to University of Oxford’s ICCS program (proposal and CV required)
past_recipients: Past fellows from Nigeria, Kenya, etc., spent terms at Oxford to develop conservation projects
geographic_focus: Africa (applicants must be working in African conservation)
gotchas: Must secure an Oxford faculty mentor for the fellowship period; English proficiency required
additional_notes: Leventis Fellowship covers course fees, accommodation, travel to Oxford for selected African conservationists

funding_name: Leakey Foundation – Field School Scholarship (Joan C. Donner Fund)
funding_amount: Up to US$2,000 toward field school tuition
funding_focus: Training in fieldwork related to human origins research (anthropology, paleoanthropology)
org_type: Students (undergrad or grad) from countries with limited resources for academic development; nomination by field school director required
Application Process: Field school director submits application on behalf of student
past_recipients: Recent recipients include students from developing countries attending paleoanthropology field schools in Africa
gotchas: Student cannot apply directly – must be recommended by field school organizer
additional_notes: Supports building capacity in human evolution research; part of Leakey Foundation’s educational programs

funding_name: Harvard University – Edward O. Wilson Biodiversity Postdoctoral Fellowship
funding_amount: US$65,000/year stipend + $5,000/year research and travel allowance
funding_focus: Taxonomy and systematics research to discover and describe Earth’s animal species
org_type: Ph.D. required; open to U.S. and non-U.S. citizens with relevant taxonomic research experience
Application Process: Submit application to Harvard MCZ (cover letter, research proposal, CV, letters of reference)
past_recipients: Inaugural fellowship (no recipients yet, launched 2025)
geographic_focus: Worldwide (fellows based at Harvard in Cambridge, MA)
gotchas: Must secure a Harvard faculty sponsor; focus on species discovery (taxonomy-centric)
additional_notes: Named after E.O. Wilson; aims to advance biodiversity knowledge by funding taxonomists

funding_name: Neotropical Birding and Conservation Grants
funding_amount: US$1,500 or $3,000 (standard grants); up to $5,000 (Juan Mazar Barnett Award)
funding_focus: Research and conservation projects benefiting Neotropical birds (incl. expeditions)
org_type: Conservationists and researchers who are nationals/residents of Neotropical countries (Caribbean, Central & South America)
Application Process: Submit application (guidelines in English/Spanish on NBC website)
past_recipients: Past grantees include projects on endemic birds in the Andes and Caribbean island species
gotchas: Early-career conservationists encouraged (Juan Mazar award is specifically for early-career)
additional_notes: Club membership not required but encouraged; program formerly known under Neotropical Bird Club conservation awards

funding_name: OceanHub Africa Startup Accelerator
funding_amount: In-kind support (6-month acceleration: mentorship, services, investor network; no direct cash grant)
funding_focus: Scaling African startups focused on ocean preservation and sustainable ocean economy (e.g. solutions to climate change, pollution, overfishing)
org_type: For-profit startups based in Africa with clear ocean impact focus (early-stage, scalable businesses)
Application Process: Online application via VC4A platform (pitch deck and business info required)
past_recipients: Cohort examples: startups in plastic waste recycling in Senegal, sustainable aquaculture in Kenya (2021 cohort)
gotchas: No equity taken but startups should be investment-ready; must commit to 6-month virtual program
additional_notes: Provides network of ocean mentors, potential seed funding exposure, and partnership opportunities

funding_name: International Nature Image Festival (FIIN) – Biodiversity Short Film Contest
grant_funder: Festival Internacional de Imagen de la Naturaleza (FIIN)
funding_focus: Short films (5–28 min) showcasing natural heritage, ecosystems, habitats, or species (wild flora/fauna)
org_type: Open to filmmakers worldwide; all genres accepted (documentary, fiction, animation, experimental, music video)
Application Process: Submit film via FIIN website (online entry form)
past_recipients: Past winning films include documentaries on Iberian lynx, Amazon rainforest (winners from multiple countries)
gotchas: Films must focus on biodiversity/nature; time limit 28 minutes; max two films per entrant
additional_notes: Part of a larger nature image festival in Portugal; also features photo contests, etc.

funding_name: Skål International Sustainable Tourism Awards
funding_amount: No direct funding (recognition award; publicity and trophy)
funding_focus: Sustainable and responsible tourism initiatives (nine categories, including “Countryside and Biodiversity” and “Marine and Coastal”)
org_type: Companies, NGOs, government agencies, and educational institutions worldwide with tourism projects in eligible categories
Application Process: Online submission of project details per award guidelines on Skål site
past_recipients: Past winners include ecotourism lodges, community-based tourism in wildlife areas, etc.
gotchas: Primarily an honor; used to raise visibility of winners’ projects; must be related to tourism
additional_notes: One of the few global tourism awards emphasizing biodiversity conservation in tourism operations

funding_name: Weeden Foundation – Biodiversity Grants (Chile & Russia)
application_deadline: 02 May 2025 (next proposal deadline; LOI at least 1 month prior)
funding_focus: Biodiversity conservation in forest and freshwater ecosystems (Patagonia region of Chile; Altai Republic of Russia)
org_type: Experienced local conservation NGOs in target regions (Chile, Russia) with projects in forest, river, or aquatic habitat protection
Application Process: Email a Letter of Inquiry; if invited, submit full proposal by deadline
past_recipients: e.g., Fundación Patagonia Sur in Chile and Arkhar NGO in Altai have received Weeden grants in the past
gotchas: LOI required well in advance; foundation rarely funds outside these focal regions
additional_notes: Foundation prioritizes projects that secure long-term habitat protection (e.g., land purchase, reserve creation)

funding_name: Fondation Franklinia – Threatened Tree Conservation
funding_amount: Not specified fixed amount (budgets must be “reasonable”; co-funding of 20–50% required)
funding_focus: In-situ conservation of globally threatened tree species (as per IUCN Red List)
org_type: Organizations worldwide with proven expertise in plant conservation; projects in Latin America or Caribbean emphasized
Application Process: Email project proposal (in English or French) per foundation guidelines
past_recipients: Past recipients include botanic gardens and NGOs conserving Magnolias in Colombia, oaks in Haiti, etc.
geographic_focus: Primarily Latin America & Caribbean (projects in other regions also considered if on Red List species)
gotchas: Requires 20–50% matching funds from other sources
additional_notes: Focused exclusively on tree species conservation; named after Sir John Franklinia (fictional context of foundation name)

funding_name: EJN Virtual Workshop – Great Apes & One Health (Africa)
funding_amount: N/A for workshop (participants get training); story grants available after workshop
funding_focus: Capacity-building for environmental journalists on great ape conservation and health (One Health) issues
org_type: Journalists in African great ape range countries (focus on those reporting on conservation and health threats to apes)
Application Process: Apply via EJN site; attend 3-day virtual workshop; then eligible to pitch for story grant
past_recipients: Not applicable (workshop with later grant opportunity; 16 journalists selected in previous workshops received follow-on grants)
geographic_focus: Africa (great ape range countries in West, Central, East Africa)
gotchas: Must attend all sessions to qualify for post-workshop grant opportunity
additional_notes: Emphasizes disease threats to apes (e.g., Ebola) and human-wildlife health link; collaboration with researchers included

funding_name: FAO International Year of Camelids Photo Contest
funding_amount: Prize: Trip to FAO HQ in Rome for winner (travel covered)
funding_focus: Raising awareness of camelid species (e.g., llamas, alpacas, camels) through photography
org_type: Amateur and professional photographers worldwide, age 18+
Application Process: Submit photos via FAO contest portal by deadline
past_recipients: N/A (first time contest held for Intl. Year of Camelids 2024/2025)
geographic_focus: Worldwide (focus on regions with camelids – South America, Middle East, Central Asia)
gotchas: No monetary award; winner travels to camelid event in Rome
additional_notes: Ties into UN-declared International Year of Camelids; highlights cultural and ecological importance of camelids

funding_name: African Bird Club – Conservation & Expedition Awards
funding_amount: Up to £3,000 (Conservation Award); up to £5,000 (Expedition Award)
funding_focus: Small to mid-scale projects on African bird conservation; Expeditions with strong bird research and conservation elements
org_type: Conservation Awards: usually African residents; Expedition Awards: researchers of any nationality for work in Africa
Application Process: Application form via ABC website; deadlines end of Feb, June, Oct (reviews after each)
past_recipients: Past funded projects: surveys of endangered Grey-necked Picathartes in Ghana; expeditions to study Madagascar forest birds
gotchas: Preference to African nationals for Conservation Awards; must have a strong conservation aspect
additional_notes: ABC also provides equipment and ringing (banding) grants; encourages capacity building of local researchers

funding_name: British Ecological Society – Outreach & Engagement Grants
funding_focus: Public engagement projects to promote ecological science to wide audiences
org_type: Individuals or organizations (researchers, educators, community groups, etc.). BES membership not required for outreach grants
Application Process: Apply via BES website (proposal outlining outreach event or activity)
past_recipients: Past recipients: museum ecology exhibits, community bioblitz events in UK, school outreach in Africa
gotchas: Must target a non-academic audience and communicate ecology; grants cannot support research itself
additional_notes: BES also offers separate grants for research; Outreach grants specifically for engagement events

funding_name: Journalismfund.eu – Environmental Journalism Development Grants
funding_amount: Total ~€115,000 to distribute (individual project budgets vary)
funding_focus: Supporting capacity-building, training, and services for investigative environmental journalism (projects, networks, conferences)
org_type: Legal entities (organizations, NGOs, media institutions) with expertise in investigative journalism, preferably in Europe
Application Process: Submit proposal via Journalismfund.eu grant portal
past_recipients: Past grantees include media training organizations in Eastern Europe developing cross-border environmental investigations
geographic_focus: Primarily Europe (projects must benefit environmental journalism in Europe)
gotchas: Not for individual story funding – must be meta-journalism projects (training, network-building)
additional_notes: Focus on enabling services (not content creation directly); encourages collaborative approaches

funding_name: Oak Spring Garden Foundation – Plant Conservation Biology Fellowship
funding_amount: US$10,000 grant + 2–8 week residency at Oak Spring estate (Virginia, USA)
funding_focus: Plant and landscape conservation projects by early-career practitioners
org_type: Early-career practitioners/scholars in plant conservation, not enrolled in undergraduate program during fellowship year
Application Process: Online application via OSGF site (project proposal, resume)
past_recipients: Inaugural fellowship awarded in 2021 to a botanist working on native prairie restoration
geographic_focus: Worldwide (no nationality restriction; residency in USA required during fellowship)
gotchas: Fellow must reside on-site for 2–8 weeks; timeline to be arranged within fellowship year
additional_notes: Includes access to Oak Spring’s gardens and library; one fellow selected per year

funding_name: Oak Spring Garden Foundation – Botanical Art Residency
funding_focus: Creation of scientifically accurate botanical artwork inspired by plant species and landscapes
org_type: Early-career botanical artists worldwide, not enrolled in undergrad during 2026
Application Process: Apply via OSGF website (portfolio and statement required)
past_recipients: Recent resident artists created illustrations of Oak Spring’s garden flora; program started 2020
geographic_focus: Worldwide (residency at Oak Spring, Virginia USA)
gotchas: Must spend residency during spring bloom season; art created may be used by OSGF
additional_notes: Combines art and science; residents have access to on-site gardens for inspiration

funding_name: Oak Spring Garden Foundation – Interdisciplinary Residency
funding_focus: Support for artists, scientists, writers, conservation practitioners working on projects inspired by plants, gardens, or landscapes
org_type: Individuals (eight per session) including researchers, artists, writers, etc. whose work relates to plants and nature; not in undergrad
Application Process: Apply via OSGF site (project description required); multiple residencies scheduled per year
past_recipients: Past participants include a mix of poets, ecologists, landscape architects working on plant-inspired projects
gotchas: Participants are in residence together (cohort of 8); must engage in group activities and share progress
additional_notes: Fosters collaboration across disciplines; residency located at historic Oak Spring estate of Rachel “Bunny” Mellon

funding_name: European Outdoor Conservation Association (EOCA) – Conservation Project Grants
funding_focus: Field projects that benefit biodiversity in wild landscapes (mountains, forests, wetlands, coasts) and involve outdoor enthusiasts or local communities
org_type: Non-profit organizations worldwide (except North America) with conservation projects (1–2 year duration)
Application Process: Online application during call window; shortlisted projects may be voted on by EOCA members/public
past_recipients: Past funded: alpine meadow restoration in Kyrgyzstan, beach clean-ups in Indonesia, wetland protection in Romania
gotchas: Projects must have tangible volunteer or community engagement and outdoor sector relevance
additional_notes: Funding comes from European outdoor gear companies; public vote often helps select winners from finalists

funding_name: GBIF Graduate Researchers Award
funding_amount: €5,000 each to two students (one Master's, one PhD)
application_deadline: 27 June 2025 (nomination deadline; some countries set earlier internal deadlines)
funding_focus: Innovative research in biodiversity informatics using GBIF data
org_type: Master’s and doctoral students enrolled at institutions in GBIF participant countries; must be nominated by national GBIF Head of Delegation
Application Process: Students prepare proposal and get nomination through their country’s GBIF delegation
past_recipients: 2023 awardees: a PhD student mapping global bat diversity (Brazil) and an MSc student studying invasive plants (Kenya)
gotchas: Requires coordination with national GBIF Node; each country can nominate up to 2 candidates
additional_notes: Promotes use of open biodiversity data; winners present research at a GBIF conference

funding_name: WWF Nepal Conservation Awards
funding_amount: NRs. 50,000 for individuals; NRs. 100,000 for organizations (approximately US$400–$800)
funding_focus: Recognition of significant contributions to biodiversity conservation in Nepal (wildlife, forests, etc.)
org_type: Nepali individuals and grassroots organizations working in nature conservation or natural resource management
Application Process: Nomination process (candidates can be nominated or self-nominate with endorsement)
past_recipients: Past honorees include community forest user groups, anti-poaching units, and conservation educators in Nepal
gotchas: Only Nepali citizens/organizations eligible; focus on on-the-ground impact
additional_notes: Up to three awards given annually (typically two individuals and one organization)

funding_name: New England Biolabs Foundation – Grassroots Conservation Grants
funding_focus: Community-based biodiversity conservation, ecosystem services, sustainable livelihoods, and marine resource conservation
org_type: Small grassroots nonprofits in specific regions: Central America, Andean South America, West Africa (see NEBF site for eligible countries)
Application Process: Submit brief Letter of Inquiry; selected organizations invited to submit full proposal
past_recipients: Past recipients: mangrove restoration groups in Honduras, agroforestry projects in Ghana, community marine reserves in Costa Rica
geographic_focus: Central America, Northern Andes Amazon, West Africa (target regions)
gotchas: Two-stage application; only organizations in designated focal ecoregions considered
additional_notes: Emphasis on grassroots organizations that might lack access to larger funding; often supports indigenous community initiatives

funding_name: British Herpetological Society – Student Research Grants
funding_focus: Herpetology fieldwork and research expenses, especially for projects benefiting conservation of reptiles or amphibians
org_type: Current students (undergraduate or postgraduate) conducting herpetological research; worldwide (though those in well-funded countries may be at slight disadvantage)
Application Process: Apply via BHS website form; BHS membership encouraged but not required
past_recipients: Have supported student projects on frog habitat use in India, tortoise ecology in Nigeria, etc.
gotchas: Preference to students from or working in countries where research funds are scarce
additional_notes: Small grants intended as seed money; students often leverage BHS grant to obtain additional funding

funding_name: GBIF Ebbe Nielsen Challenge 2025
funding_focus: Innovative tools or techniques to improve access, utility, or quality of open biodiversity data
org_type: Individuals, teams, companies, or governmental agencies worldwide; open to anyone except GBIF staff
Application Process: Submit project idea/solution online (concept note, demo, or prototype) by deadline
past_recipients: 2024 winners developed an AI tool to flag data errors in museum records and a mobile app for citizen scientists
gotchas: Solution must use or enhance GBIF-mediated data; open science focus
additional_notes: Multiple winners or one winner – GBIF decides allocation of the €20k among top entries; recognition at GBIF Global Nodes meeting

funding_name: Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund
grant_funder: Mohamed bin Zayed Species Conservation Fund
application_deadline: 28 Feb, 30 June, 31 Oct 2025 (three cycles a year)
funding_focus: Conservation of threatened species (any plant, animal, fungi) worldwide, especially lesser-known and highly endangered species
org_type: Open to anyone (individuals, communities, organizations) with a project on Critically Endangered or Endangered species (per IUCN)
Application Process: Online application form (in English) on fund website; simple proposal outlining species, threats, actions
past_recipients: Since 2009, has funded over 2,250 projects e.g., Siamese crocodile surveys in Lao PDR, orchid conservation in Brazil
gotchas: Focus on IUCN-listed CR/EN species; will consider Data Deficient or lesser-known species too; grants often around $10k on average
additional_notes: Provides rapid, flexible small grants; high volume of applications each round

funding_name: Panthera – Wild Cats Conservation Grants
funding_amount: Up to US$15,000 (Small Cat Action Fund); US$10,000 fellowship
funding_focus: Research and conservation of wild cat species, especially small cats; and a special fellowship for field experience
org_type: Researchers and conservationists worldwide focusing on wild cats; early-career conservationists for fellowship
Application Process: Submit Letter of Interest for Small Cat Action Fund and Winston Cobb Fellowship via Panthera’s portal
past_recipients: Previous Small Cat grantees worked on fishing cats in Sri Lanka, Andean cat in Bolivia; fellowship recipients train on big cat projects
geographic_focus: Worldwide (projects can be anywhere wild cats exist)
gotchas: “Small Cats” fund excludes lions, tigers, etc.; fellowship requires an internship on a Panthera project
additional_notes: Panthera also runs separate grants for tiger and lion conservation via partnerships; this fund fills gap for under-studied small felids

funding_name: Monarch Butterfly Fund – Lincoln Brower Award
funding_focus: Research on monarch butterfly conservation and habitat (e.g., forest ecology in Mexico, migratory studies)
org_type: Undergraduate or graduate students conducting monarch-related research (global, but often North America/Mexico focus)
Application Process: Apply by proposal to MBF (via email or form) outlining research objectives and budget
past_recipients: 2022 winner studied milkweed restoration in California; past recipients often from U.S. or Mexico
gotchas: Must directly relate to monarch butterfly conservation; stipend mainly for research expenses
additional_notes: Named after Dr. Lincoln Brower, renowned monarch expert; encourages next-gen monarch researchers

funding_name: American Assoc. of Zoo Veterinarians – Wild Animal Health Fund (Travel Grants)
funding_amount: Up to US$2,000 for conference travel
funding_focus: Financial aid for zoo/wildlife veterinarians from developing countries to attend AAZV annual conference
org_type: Zoo and wildlife veterinarians outside the USA (especially from developing nations) with demonstrated need and conservation goals
Application Process: Submit application with CV and statement of need via AAZV website
past_recipients: Examples: vets from Kenya and Indonesia received grants to present conservation case studies at AAZV conference
gotchas: Must detail how conference attendance benefits conservation in home country; preference to first-time attendees
additional_notes: Part of AAZV’s Wild Animal Health Fund efforts to build global veterinary capacity

funding_name: Elephant Managers Association – Small Grants
funding_focus: Field-based elephant conservation projects in Africa or Asia; emphasis on community outreach, capacity building, and captive management improvement
org_type: Anyone (including zookeepers, field conservationists, researchers) with a project addressing urgent elephant issues in range countries
Application Process: Submit application form (download from EMA site) by email
past_recipients: Recent winners: human-elephant conflict mitigation in Sri Lanka; elephant sanctuary enrichment in Kenya
gotchas: Projects with strong community or husbandry component prioritized; open to non-members
additional_notes: Funded by zoo professionals’ association; aims to bridge ex situ and in situ elephant care and conservation

funding_name: Tusk Conservation Awards (Prince William Award etc.)
funding_focus: Recognizes outstanding African conservation leaders: Lifetime achievement, significant impact, and rangers on the ground
org_type: Individuals working in conservation in Africa (conservation leaders, wildlife rangers) – must be nominated by a third party
Application Process: Nomination via Tusk Awards website (detailed form and references)
past_recipients: 2022 winners included a Namibian elephant conservation pioneer and a Zambian community conservation leader
gotchas: Not an open grant: it’s a prestigious award; nominees should have 10+ years of accomplishment
additional_notes: Three main awards: Prince William Award (£100k), Tusk Award (£75k), Wildlife Ranger Award (£30k)

funding_name: Patagonia Environmental Grants Program
funding_focus: Action-oriented, root-cause environmental projects, including biodiversity protection and advocacy
org_type: Environmental nonprofit organizations. Regions: primarily U.S., Canada, Europe; in developing world, only Chile and Argentina currently eligible
Application Process: Online application on Patagonia’s grant portal; requires proposal and financials
past_recipients: Patagonia has funded groups like Save the Colorado, Ecosistemas (Chile), and grassroots anti-dam campaigns in Europe
geographic_focus: North America, Europe; limited support in Chile & Argentina for Latin America
gotchas: Only non-profit, activist groups; company prefers to fund campaigns addressing root causes (not just species research)
additional_notes: Patagonia’s grants are part of its 1% for the Planet commitment; often renew support for effective grantees

funding_name: Turtle Conservation Fund – Small Grants
funding_focus: Conservation and research of endangered and critically endangered tortoise and freshwater turtle species
org_type: Individuals and organizations worldwide working on TCF priority species (list of species provided by TCF)
Application Process: Apply via TCF website (proposal form); two cycles per year
past_recipients: Multiple small grants awarded each cycle – e.g., projects on Radiated Tortoise in Madagascar, Central American river turtle in Belize
gotchas: Priority to species classified as Critically Endangered, Endangered, or highly threatened; must align with TCF’s priority list
additional_notes: A partnership initiative of several turtle conservation NGOs; aims to provide rapid support to urgent turtle projects

funding_name: American Society of Primatologists – Conservation Small Grants
funding_focus: Primatological research or conservation projects (including captive care improvements) with direct benefit to primate conservation
org_type: Students and early-career researchers, especially from primate range countries (or projects involving those countries)
Application Process: Submit proposal to ASP Conservation Committee (via ASP website)
past_recipients: Recently funded: community education to protect chimps in Senegal; study of spider monkey habitat in Ecuador
geographic_focus: Primarily Africa, Asia, Latin America (primate range countries)
gotchas: Membership in ASP not required but helpful; priority to projects led by nationals of habitat countries
additional_notes: Grants can support field supplies, student stipends, etc.; part of ASP’s effort to promote global primate conservation

funding_name: Raptor Research Foundation – Grants & Awards
funding_focus: Research on birds of prey (raptors) – multiple grant categories for research, education, and conference travel
org_type: Students and professionals (both members and non-members of RRF) conducting raptor research; each award has specific criteria
Application Process: Submit applications to RRF Awards Committee; format and requirements differ per award (see RRF website)
past_recipients: Examples: The Leslie Brown Memorial Grant helped fund an eagle research project in Kenya; the Amadon Grant supported a hawk migration study in India
gotchas: Some awards restricted to RRF members, others open to all; must pertain to raptor conservation or research
additional_notes: Multiple named awards (Amadon, Tully, etc.) focus on different aspects (e.g., youth research, developing country researchers, etc.)

funding_name: Club300 Foundation for Bird Protection
funding_focus: Research or conservation of the world’s most threatened and poorly known bird species (Critically Endangered, Endangered, Data Deficient)
org_type: Researchers and conservationists worldwide focusing on bird species classified as CR, EN, EW or Data Deficient on IUCN Red List
Application Process: Apply by sending proposal (in English or Swedish) to Club300 Foundation by deadline
past_recipients: Recent grants: discovered new population of Stresemann’s Bristlefront in Brazil; community conservation of Cebu Flowerpecker in Philippines
gotchas: Projects must target species in specific IUCN categories (no funding for lower-risk species)
additional_notes: Foundation run by birders; funds ~5 projects per year; heavy emphasis on tangible conservation outcomes

funding_name: WIOMSA – Marine Conservation Management (CORDIO program)
grant_funder: Western Indian Ocean Marine Science Association (WIOMSA)
funding_amount: Support for training/workshop (no direct grant money to individuals)
funding_focus: Building capacity in marine protected area (MPA) management and marine conservation in Western Indian Ocean
org_type: MPA practitioners, managers, researchers from WIOMSA member countries (East Africa, island states in Indian Ocean)
Application Process: Apply through WIOMSA when calls open (e.g., for workshops or scholarship programs)
past_recipients: For instance, WIOMSA’s Marine Research Grant supported coral reef resilience studies in Tanzania
geographic_focus: Western Indian Ocean region (East Africa, Madagascar, Seychelles, etc.)
gotchas: Programs often involve attending regional training or receiving small research funds; must be from member countries
additional_notes: Often done in partnership with organizations like CORDIO and CORDAP (Coral Reef programs)

funding_name: IUCN ‘Nature+’ Climate-Positive Projects (Water & Climate)
funding_focus: Innovative projects linking biodiversity and climate change (Nature-based Solutions that are ‘nature positive’)
org_type: NGOs, civil society, and local communities in IUCN focal countries (often developing countries)
Application Process: Apply via IUCN call for proposals (usually concept note then full proposal)
past_recipients: Examples: mangrove restoration for climate adaptation in West Africa funded under previous IUCN grants
geographic_focus: Global (especially Asia, Africa, LatAm – varies by call)
gotchas: Usually requires multi-stakeholder partnerships; rigorous M&E framework
additional_notes: ‘Nature+’ is part of IUCN’s program branding; these grants often funded by bilateral donors

funding_name: Jana Robeyst Trust Fund – Small Conservation Grants (Africa)
grant_funder: Jana Robeyst Trust Fund for Small Conservation Projects
funding_focus: Small projects and studies on African wildlife conservation (priority to elephant-related projects, but not exclusive)
org_type: Early-career researchers, students and small NGOs from Africa or doing work in Africa; project budget under €1,500
Application Process: Simple application by email (description, budget, CV) to JRTF by deadline
past_recipients: Has funded projects like elephant corridor surveys in Tanzania, primate conservation education in DR Congo
gotchas: Applicants should be under 40 or small organizations; preference for projects with immediate practical conservation impact
additional_notes: One of few micro-grants specifically for African researchers; named in memory of Jana Robeyst

funding_name: Arcus Foundation – Great Apes & Gibbons Program
funding_amount: Typically US$50,000 – $150,000 (can vary; large foundation grants)
application_deadline: Concept notes usually due March (invitation only in many cases)
funding_focus: Conservation of great apes (gorillas, chimpanzees, bonobos) and gibbons; includes habitat protection and advocacy
org_type: Organizations (NGOs, research institutions) working in ape range countries in Africa and Southeast Asia
Application Process: By invitation or inquiry; Arcus often solicits proposals in focal regions (no open call on website)
past_recipients: Arcus has supported grantees like WCS for Cross River gorilla protection, Fauna & Flora International for gibbon conservation
geographic_focus: Central & West Africa (great apes), Southeast Asia (gibbons)
gotchas: Arcus does not accept unsolicited proposals; networking needed to receive invitation
additional_notes: Arcus also supports LGBT human rights; their Great Apes program is one of the world’s major private funding sources for ape conservation

funding_name: Marisla Foundation – Marine Conservation Grants
funding_focus: Marine biodiversity conservation (oceans), with secondary focus on toxic pollution issues
org_type: US and international NGOs active in marine conservation or pollution reduction; many grants in North America and Pacific regions
Application Process: Unsolicited letters of inquiry accepted by mail; foundation invites full proposals for promising LOIs
past_recipients: Funds large initiatives e.g., marine protected area establishment in California, coral reef protection in Pacific Islands
Contact Information: No public website (Marisla info via Foundation Directory)
geographic_focus: Primarily USA and Pacific Basin; also some Latin America
gotchas: Low-profile family foundation; prefers existing partners; no online presence
additional_notes: Formerly the Homeland Foundation; funded by an oil heiress, major supporter of Oceana and NRDC, etc.

funding_name: EJN Ocean Conference Fellowships 2025
funding_amount: Travel, accommodation, and training support to attend UN Ocean Conference 2025
application_deadline: December 2024 (for 2025 UN Ocean Conference in Nice)
funding_focus: Enabling journalists to report on the UN Ocean Conference and ocean conservation issues
org_type: Journalists from developing countries or small island states, especially those covering marine issues
Application Process: Online application to EJN; includes story pitch related to Ocean Conference themes
past_recipients: In 2022, EJN sponsored 14 journalists to attend the UN Ocean conference in Lisbon, resulting in dozens of published stories
geographic_focus: Global (with focus on reporters from countries most affected by ocean issues)
gotchas: Must produce stories during/after the conference; strong English skills required
additional_notes: Provides mentorship during conference; aims to raise profile of under-reported ocean issues in local media

funding_name: Mongabay – Conservation Reporting Fellowships
application_deadline: Calls open periodically (e.g., July 2024 for 2025 fellows)
funding_focus: Environmental journalism experience covering conservation topics; fellows write articles for Mongabay
org_type: Early-career journalists, often from tropical countries, interested in environmental reporting
Application Process: Apply via Mongabay portal with writing samples and pitches
past_recipients: Past fellows have produced series on deforestation in the Amazon, wildlife trade in Southeast Asia (published on mongabay.com)
geographic_focus: Global (recent cohorts focused on Indonesia, India, Latin America)
gotchas: Fellows must publish a set number of articles on Mongabay during fellowship; intensive editorial support provided
additional_notes: Focus on capacity building – many fellows continue as regular environmental journalists in their regions

funding_name: American Ornithological Society – Student/Postdoc Research Awards
funding_focus: Research in ornithology (any aspect of bird biology, including conservation) by students and postdoctoral researchers
org_type: Graduate students or postdoctoral researchers who are AOS members (membership required)
Application Process: Submit research proposal via AOS online system (annual call)
past_recipients: AOS grant recipients have studied topics like migratory songbird stopover ecology, effects of climate on breeding timing
geographic_focus: Worldwide (no restriction on study location; membership is international)
gotchas: Must be AOS member in good standing; many awards named after eminent ornithologists
additional_notes: Multiple awards available (e.g., Chapman Grant, Nelson Grant) administered under one application process; highly competitive

funding_name: GBIF Capacity Enhancement Support Program (CESP)
funding_focus: Capacity building projects to enhance biodiversity data publishing and use in GBIF participant countries
org_type: GBIF Participant nodes (national biodiversity data institutions) in eligible countries, often in partnerships
Application Process: Apply through GBIF country nodes; proposals should involve at least two countries (node-to-node collaboration)
past_recipients: E.g., a 2021 CESP grant trained biodiversity data managers in Spanish-speaking Latin American countries
geographic_focus: Global (GBIF member countries, especially developing nodes)
gotchas: Must be led by GBIF Node or partner; at least two countries collaborate
additional_notes: Aims to transfer skills between countries – e.g., mentoring between a mature node and a newer node in data mobilization

funding_name: Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund – Caribbean Islands Hotspot
funding_amount: Up to US$150,000 for large grants (and small grants ~$50k)
application_deadline: Late 2024 (e.g., LOIs due 1 Dec 2024 for Caribbean call)
funding_focus: Biodiversity conservation in Caribbean Islands Hotspot – key biodiversity areas, species protection, livelihoods
org_type: Local NGOs, CSOs, communities in Caribbean islands (Dominican Rep., Haiti, Jamaica, etc.), regional NGOs
Application Process: Submit Letter of Inquiry in CEPF portal; selected LOIs invited to full proposal
past_recipients: CEPF Caribbean funded creation of Haiti’s first private nature reserve; community ecotourism in Jamaica, etc.
gotchas: Strictly must address priorities in CEPF’s Caribbean ecosystem profile; local implementing organizations favored
additional_notes: CEPF is jointly funded by multiple donors (World Bank, Japan, EU, etc.); focuses on civil society role in conservation

funding_name: Disney Conservation Fund – Annual Conservation Grants
grant_funder: Disney Conservation Fund (Disney Worldwide Services, Inc.)
funding_focus: Community-based wildlife conservation projects worldwide; emphasis on connecting kids and communities with nature
org_type: Registered nonprofit conservation organizations with projects in site-based wildlife conservation, community engagement, or education
Application Process: Online application by invitation (applicants first submit inquiry; selected organizations invited to full proposal)
past_recipients: Has supported ~600 organizations in 120+ countries (e.g., International Rhino Foundation, Jane Goodall Institute projects)
geographic_focus: Worldwide (projects in 1+ of Disney’s focus regions globally)
gotchas: Highly competitive; must have measurable outcomes and typically involve Disney employee engagement or collaboration
additional_notes: Since 1995, Disney has contributed over $125 million to conservation initiatives globally; grants often renewed for successful programs

funding_name: Whitley Awards (Whitley Fund for Nature)
funding_amount: £40,000 to winner (Whitley Award); additional £100,000 available for follow-on projects
funding_focus: Recognizes effective grassroots conservation leaders in the Global South (“Green Oscars”)
org_type: Dynamic mid-career conservationists leading NGOs or notable projects in their home country (especially in biodiversity-rich developing countries)
Application Process: Nomination process (candidates typically nominated by an associate; rigorous review and interview)
past_recipients: Recent Whitley Award winners include conservation leaders protecting snow leopards in Mongolia, sea turtles in Nicaragua
gotchas: Winners must attend ceremony in London; prize money must be spent on agreed conservation activities
additional_notes: Prestige award with significant media exposure; winners join international network and can compete for Continuation Funding of up to £100k

funding_name: Rufford Small Grants for Nature Conservation
funding_amount: £5,000 initial grant; £10,000, £15,000, £25,000 possible in subsequent stages
funding_focus: Pilot-scale or small conservation projects in developing countries
org_type: Early-career conservationists (often local project leaders) in developing countries; project budget < £5,000 for first grant
Application Process: Apply online to Rufford Foundation; successful projects can reapply for 2nd, 3rd, 4th stage grants progressively
past_recipients: Over 5,000 projects funded worldwide – e.g., tiger human-conflict mitigation in India (Stage 1), expanded to landscape level by Stage 3
geographic_focus: Developing countries in Asia, Africa, Latin America, E. Europe
gotchas: Must complete project and report to advance to next funding stage; strong emphasis on on-ground impact and community involvement
additional_notes: Well-known stepping stone funding – many larger conservationists (e.g., Whitley Award winners) started with a Rufford Small Grant

funding_name: Prince Bernhard Nature Fund (PBNF)
funding_focus: Small, targeted conservation projects worldwide, especially in developing countries and Eastern Europe
org_type: Local NGOs and grassroots organizations with limited access to large funds; must have matching funds (~50%)
Application Process: Apply via PBNF online system with project proposal; decisions in June and December
past_recipients: Funded creation of community marine reserve in Fiji, protection of Red-crowned cranes in Russia, etc.
geographic_focus: Worldwide (priority to Africa, Asia, Latin America, Eastern Europe)
gotchas: Requires ~50% co-funding from other sources; project duration ~1 year
additional_notes: Named after Prince Bernhard of Netherlands; particularly keen on innovative, bottom-up approaches

funding_name: Conservation Leadership Programme (CLP) – Team Awards
grant_funder: CLP (BirdLife International, Fauna & Flora International, WCS, funded by BP)
funding_amount: Up to $15,000 (Future Conservationist Award); follow-up Awards $25k and $50k
funding_focus: Early-career conservation team projects on species/habitat conservation, with leadership development component
org_type: Teams of 3–5 early-career conservationists (all <5 years professional experience) from eligible developing countries
Application Process: Online application (proposal) via CLP website; future rounds by invitation for follow-up
past_recipients: Many alumni: e.g., a team in Bolivia discovered new frog species; CLP alumni have gone on to start NGOs or win Whitley Awards
geographic_focus: Global (eligible countries list mainly in Latin America, Asia, Africa, E. Europe)
gotchas: Project must be team-led and build local capacity; typically must not be for well-funded charismatic species
additional_notes: Includes international training for awardees (two-week Conservation Leadership training workshop) as part of award

funding_name: Darwin Initiative Main Projects
grant_funder: UK Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (DEFRA) – Darwin Initiative
funding_focus: Biodiversity conservation and poverty alleviation in developing countries (supporting CBD objectives)
org_type: Partnerships led by organizations (NGOs, research institutes, governments) in UK and biodiverse developing countries
Application Process: Two-stage application (Concept note, then Full proposal by invitation) via Darwin online portal
past_recipients: Examples: sustainable forestry with communities in Kenya; saving the pygmy sloth in Panama (ZSL-led project)
geographic_focus: Developing countries (must be on OECD DAC list)
gotchas: Requires UK and host country partner collaboration; must address livelihoods and biodiversity
additional_notes: Highly competitive, well-known program since 1992; also has Darwin Plus for UK overseas territories

funding_name: NFWF Conservation Grants (Various Programs)
funding_amount: Ranges widely: e.g., $50,000–$500,000+ depending on program
application_deadline: Multiple deadlines per year per program
funding_focus: Wildlife and habitat conservation in the United States and territories (programs for specific species, habitats, or regions)
org_type: US-based nonprofits, state agencies, tribes, educational institutions (sometimes international NGOs for certain programs)
Application Process: Apply via NFWF website to specific program RFP (each program has its own process)
past_recipients: Examples: NFWF’s Monarch Butterfly and Pollinators Fund gave $150k to plant milkweed in Texas; Coral Reef Conservation Fund grants in Florida, Pacific territories
geographic_focus: Primarily United States (some programs include international components, e.g., migratory bird wintering grounds)
gotchas: Most programs require non-federal matching funds (usually 1:1)
additional_notes: NFWF manages many funds with corporate partners (Shell marine fund, Walmart Acres for America, etc.) and federal funding; over $4 billion granted since 1984

funding_name: EU LIFE Programme – Nature & Biodiversity
funding_amount: No fixed maximum, often €1–5 million per project (60% co-funding from EU)
funding_focus: Large-scale projects for species, habitats, Natura 2000 sites in the EU; also biodiversity policy implementation
org_type: Consortia of NGOs, government agencies, research institutions within EU member states
Application Process: Apply via EU Funding & Tenders portal (detailed proposal, usually two-stage)
past_recipients: Numerous projects, e.g., LIFE Lynx reintroduced lynx in Alps, LIFE Danube Free Sky reducing bird collision with powerlines
geographic_focus: European Union member states and certain associated countries
gotchas: Requires substantial co-financing (at least 40%); lengthy application
additional_notes: Flagship EU funding for conservation; very competitive but high impact; also sub-programmes for Nature, Environment, Climate

funding_name: UNDP GEF Small Grants Programme (SGP)
application_deadline: Rolling (each country SGP has its own calls)
funding_focus: Community-based projects on biodiversity conservation, climate change, land degradation, sustainable forestry, etc., aligning with GEF priorities
org_type: Local NGOs, CBOs, indigenous groups in participating developing countries (SGP operates in 100+ countries)
Application Process: Apply to national SGP coordinators (proposal process managed in-country)
past_recipients: Thousands of community projects since 1992 – e.g., community turtle conservation in Fiji, beekeeping as alternative livelihood in Ghana
geographic_focus: Developing countries worldwide (each participating country has a national program)
gotchas: Decision made by National Steering Committee in each country; highly grassroots-focused
additional_notes: Often first funding for grassroots groups; supports empowerment of women, indigenous people; slogan ‘community action, global impact’

funding_name: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service – Critically Endangered Species Conservation Fund
funding_focus: Conservation of Critically Endangered species (non-US) – e.g., Asian species, African amphibians, etc., not covered by other USFWS programs
org_type: Nonprofits, researchers, government agencies worldwide (for species of critical concern globally, often lesser-known taxa)
Application Process: Apply via Grants.gov (Funding Opportunity by USFWS)
past_recipients: Funded projects like Siamese crocodile nest protection in Cambodia, vaquita monitoring in Mexico
geographic_focus: Worldwide (focus on non-US countries; species must be Critically Endangered on IUCN Red List)
gotchas: Species not eligible under other USFWS funds (which often target certain taxa like tigers, elephants) are prioritized
additional_notes: Part of USFWS Wildlife Without Borders programs; subject to US federal funding availability each year

funding_name: Conservation International – Global Conservation Fund
application_deadline: No fixed cycle (strategic investments by CI)
funding_focus: Creation and expansion of protected areas, land acquisition, and conservation agreements to protect biodiversity hotspots
org_type: Usually given to CI country offices or local partners for specific site-based projects (not an open application)
Application Process: Internal selection by CI; occasionally partners can pitch proposals via CI programs
past_recipients: E.g., CI’s fund helped establish new protected areas in Madagascar, conservation concessions in South America
geographic_focus: Global (key biodiversity areas in hotspots and wilderness areas)
gotchas: Not open to unsolicited proposals; projects align with CI’s strategic priorities
additional_notes: Capitalizes a long-term endowment for certain protected areas; often leverages matching funds from governments

funding_name: The Nature Conservancy – Small Conservation Grants (EFN)
funding_focus: Local community action grants for conservation and sustainable use (often linked to TNC priority regions)
org_type: Local NGOs and community groups in areas where TNC works (e.g., Mesoamerican reefs, Indonesian fisheries)
Application Process: Application through TNC local offices or specific calls (not central)
past_recipients: For instance, TNC’s EFN (Ecosystem Finance Network) in Mesoamerica gave small grants to community mangrove projects
gotchas: Often part of larger TNC project support; not widely advertised
additional_notes: TNC mostly does large-scale projects; any small grants are usually through special initiatives or partner programs

funding_name: Wildlife Conservation Society – Climate Adaptation Fund
grant_funder: WCS (supported by Doris Duke Charitable Foundation)
funding_focus: On-the-ground projects in U.S. that implement wildlife adaptation to climate change (e.g., habitat resilience, species movement)
org_type: U.S.-based conservation nonprofits, universities, tribal governments
Application Process: Apply via WCS proposal portal (pre-proposal, then invite full proposal)
past_recipients: Funded examples: restoring coastal wetlands in North Carolina to absorb sea-level rise; assisted migration of trees in Minnesota
gotchas: Must have clear climate adaptation intent (not just standard conservation)
additional_notes: Demonstration projects to inform broader practices; funded by a private foundation, managed by WCS

funding_name: Shell Canada – Fueling Change Grants (Shell Environmental Fund)
funding_amount: C$25,000 (formerly up to $100k split among multiple winners)
application_deadline: N/A (program currently on hold as of recent years)
funding_focus: Community environmental projects in Canada (wildlife habitat restoration, environmental education, pollution reduction)
org_type: Canadian registered charities, nonprofits, schools
Application Process: Online application when program was active; public voting component to select finalists
past_recipients: Funded in past: wetland boardwalk in Ontario, school native garden in Alberta
gotchas: Program subject to change/corporate strategy; was a CSR initiative
additional_notes: Illustrative of corporate small grant programs; current status uncertain

funding_name: Lush Cosmetics – The Lush Spring Prize (Environment & Social Regeneration)
application_deadline: February 2025 (nomination deadline, runs every two years)
funding_focus: Environmental and social regeneration projects, many related to agroecology, ecosystem restoration, biodiversity
org_type: Community projects, grassroots organizations, social enterprises globally working on regenerative approaches
Application Process: Nomination and application process (self-nomination allowed) via Spring Prize website
past_recipients: Winners included permaculture forest regeneration in Amazon, seed-saving networks in India
gotchas: Focus on holistic regeneration (soil, ecosystems, community); not strictly a conservation grant but often overlaps
additional_notes: Backed by Lush cosmetics’ philanthropy; prizes decided by judging panel; also has youth and influence awards

funding_name: National Geographic Society Grants – Exploration & Conservation
funding_focus: Cutting-edge research, conservation, storytelling or technology that addresses NatGeo’s focus areas (Wildlife, Human Journey, Oceans, etc.)
org_type: Researchers, conservationists, educators, storytellers worldwide (often Ph.D. or equivalent experience for larger grants)
Application Process: Online application via National Geographic’s grant portal; two tiers (explorer level and experienced)
past_recipients: Funded Jane Goodall in 1960s; recent grants to emerging explorers discovering new species or protecting critical landscapes
gotchas: Applicants under 40 or new to NatGeo start with Level I ($30k); must share findings via NatGeo platforms
additional_notes: Highly prestigious; grants come with the title “National Geographic Explorer” and support beyond money (media exposure, networking)

funding_name: Shell Nigeria – Niger Delta Biodiversity Project (Example CSR Grant)
funding_focus: Mangrove restoration, livelihood support, and biodiversity monitoring in Niger Delta
org_type: Local NGOs and community groups in the Niger Delta region
Application Process: Projects usually identified in partnership with Shell’s community relations teams; not openly advertised
past_recipients: One project created a community mangrove nursery and planted 50,000 mangrove seedlings in Bayelsa State
gotchas: CSR-driven, not open call; tied to mitigating oil impact on environment
additional_notes: Representative of oil company local biodiversity offsets; terms set via community MoUs

funding_name: HSBC Water Programme (FreshWater)
funding_amount: Varies (multi-million global program split among partners and local grants)
funding_focus: Freshwater ecosystem conservation (river basin management, wetland restoration) and water resources for communities
org_type: Major NGOs (WWF, Earthwatch) and local partners in target basins (e.g., Ganges, Yangtze, Pantanal)
Application Process: Through partnership – not open application; local grants managed by WWF etc. under program
past_recipients: Funded revival of marshes in China’s Yangtze basin; citizen science water monitoring via Earthwatch in UK
gotchas: Funds are disbursed via partner NGOs’ grantmaking channels
additional_notes: Illustrates corporate-NGO partnership model: large corporate funding channelled to small projects via expert NGOs

funding_name: Google.org Impact Challenge on Climate Innovation
funding_amount: Up to $5 million for top projects (multiple awards)
funding_focus: Big data and technology solutions for climate and environment, including biodiversity (monitoring, mapping)
org_type: Nonprofits, social enterprises worldwide with tech-driven projects
Application Process: Call for proposals via Google Impact Challenge site; panel selection
past_recipients: One grantee built an AI tool to identify rainforest fauna from sound recordings
gotchas: Highly competitive global call; emphasis on innovation and scalability
additional_notes: One-time or periodic challenges rather than annual; Google also provides support in tech/AI expertise

funding_name: Oracle Wildlife Grants (Example Corporate Foundation)
funding_focus: Wildlife and biodiversity protection projects, often near Oracle office communities or through zoo partnerships
org_type: Conservation nonprofits known to Oracle or recommended by employees
Application Process: Invitation-only proposals aligned with Oracle’s CSR focus
past_recipients: Oracle has funded sea turtle conservation in Costa Rica and elephant research via Wildlife Conservation Network
geographic_focus: Global (focus where Oracle operates, e.g., Americas, India)
gotchas: Not publicly advertised; often through employee engagement or existing NGO relationships
additional_notes: Typical of many corporate philanthropy programs that include environment as one focus area

funding_name: Conservation X Labs – Tech Innovation Challenges
grant_funder: Conservation X Labs (funded by various donors)
application_deadline: Periodic (e.g., Con X Tech Prize biannually)
funding_focus: New technology solutions for conservation problems (hardware, software, genetic, etc.)
org_type: Inventors, engineers, students, anyone with a prototype idea (globally)
Application Process: Enter online challenge; finalists get small grants to build prototype; winners get larger prize
past_recipients: Winning innovations: DNA barcode scanner to detect illegal timber; low-cost sensors for wildlife monitoring
gotchas: Intellectual property considerations – teams retain IP but must open-source certain aspects
additional_notes: Emphasis on scalable and disruptive innovation (often supports early prototypes that can attract further investment)

funding_name: Sustainable Agriculture Grants – Rainforest Alliance Re:generate Fund
funding_focus: Biodiversity-friendly sustainable agriculture and forest community livelihoods (especially agroforestry, certification preparation)
org_type: Farmer cooperatives, local NGOs in tropical agriculture landscapes (Latin America, Africa, Asia)
Application Process: Apply via Rainforest Alliance; proposals evaluated by multi-stakeholder committee
past_recipients: Funded projects like diversifying coffee farms with shade trees in Peru, beekeeping alongside cocoa in Ghana
geographic_focus: Select countries in Latin America, Africa, Asia (Rainforest Alliance focus regions)
gotchas: Must benefit Rainforest Alliance certification communities or similar; often requires co-investment from commodity buyers
additional_notes: Aims to drive innovation in sustainable supply chains at community level; co-funded by corporate partners in supply chains

funding_name: Keidanren Nature Conservation Fund (KNCF) Grants
funding_focus: Conservation of biodiversity in developing countries, especially Asia-Pacific; support for NGOs’ field projects
org_type: Japanese and international NGOs carrying out projects in developing countries (especially Asia)
Application Process: Apply via KNCF in Japanese or English with project proposal
past_recipients: Has supported wetland conservation in Myanmar, tiger protection in Malaysia, etc.
gotchas: Japanese NGOs encouraged to partner with local NGOs; funds often go to joint projects
additional_notes: Funded by Japan’s business federation donations; in 30+ years has funded hundreds of projects abroad

funding_name: Walmart Acres for America Program
funding_focus: Land conservation to offset Walmart’s footprint: protects wildlife habitat acres equal to development (goal: 1 acre conserved per acre developed by Walmart)
org_type: U.S. conservation organizations (land trusts, NGOs) securing land or conservation easements for biodiversity
Application Process: Apply through NFWF’s Acres for America RFP (annual)
past_recipients: Since 2005, funded projects protecting over 1.8 million acres, e.g., sagebrush steppe in Montana, longleaf pine forest in Florida
geographic_focus: United States (priority to projects with connectivity and large-scale impact)
gotchas: Requires 1:1 non-federal match; must benefit priority species and allow public access when possible
additional_notes: Flagship example of corporate-funded habitat conservation at landscape scale; partnership with NFWF ensures scientific rigor

funding_name: EU BEST 2.0+ (Biodiversity in EU Overseas Territories)
funding_focus: Biodiversity conservation and sustainable development in European Overseas Territories (Pacific, Caribbean, Indian Ocean, etc.)
org_type: Local NGOs, authorities, communities in EU overseas entities (e.g., New Caledonia, French Polynesia, Caribbean islands)
Application Process: Apply via EU funding portal when calls open (often one call per region per year)
past_recipients: Projects like invasive species removal on Galápagos (Ecuador EU OT), coral restoration in New Caledonia funded
gotchas: Must involve local stakeholders; part of EU’s voluntary scheme, so less bureaucratic than LIFE
additional_notes: Provides lifeline funding in small islands and territories that aren’t eligible for other international funds due to political status

funding_name: Rapid Response Facility (RRF) – Emergency Funding for World Heritage Sites
funding_focus: Emergency support for Natural World Heritage sites facing acute threats (poaching outbreaks, natural disasters, etc.)
org_type: Managers of UNESCO Natural World Heritage Sites or NGOs working with them
Application Process: Simple rapid application via email to RRF; quick internal review
past_recipients: Used for anti-poaching patrol surge in Garamba (DRC), rebuilding conservation infrastructure after a hurricane in Galápagos
geographic_focus: Global (Natural World Heritage Sites in developing countries)
gotchas: Must demonstrate immediate need and that action would substantially mitigate threat; follow-up reporting required
additional_notes: Donor-funded facility (FFI, UNESCO, etc.); small but critical funds often mobilized within 1-2 weeks

funding_name: Wildlife Emergency Fund – Rainforest Trust
funding_focus: Emergency interventions to save wildlife in imminent crisis (e.g., land purchase to stop imminent habitat destruction, rescue of populations)
org_type: Trusted conservation partners of Rainforest Trust worldwide (must be vetted; not open to general public)
Application Process: Partners alert Rainforest Trust of emergency; expedited approval if criteria met
past_recipients: E.g., emergency land acquisition in Ecuador to prevent mining, funding ranger operations after sudden deforestation spike in Cameroon
gotchas: Rainforest Trust covers 100% of urgent project cost quickly, but partner must implement fast; only existing partners can access
additional_notes: Complements RT’s regular land conservation projects by addressing unforeseeable urgent needs

funding_name: Rapid Action Grants – IUCN SOS (Save Our Species)
grant_funder: IUCN Save Our Species (funded by EU, private)
funding_focus: Enabling swift conservation actions for species facing sudden threats or opportunities (any taxon)
org_type: NGOs, CSOs, research institutions in eligible countries (mostly Africa, Asia, Latin America)
Application Process: Online application with simplified format for rapid review by IUCN SOS
past_recipients: Supported emergency response to disease outbreak in saiga antelope, averting illegal fishing spikes in Malawi during COVID, etc.
geographic_focus: Global (specific focus varies by funding source; often African wildlife)
gotchas: Project duration usually <12 months; must address an immediate threat or time-bound opportunity
additional_notes: Funded by EU’s African Wildlife Initiative and others; part of larger SOS fund which also has larger grants

funding_name: Conservation Allies – Micro Grants
funding_focus: Tiny grants to grassroots wildlife conservation projects (often for equipment or urgent needs)
org_type: Small, nascent NGOs or community groups in developing countries with which Conservation Allies has a relationship
Application Process: Informal application (often via referral or email)
past_recipients: Examples: funded fuel for patrols in a Nigerian primate sanctuary, built beehive fences for elephants in India (in partnership with local NGOs)
gotchas: Invitation or referral only; very quick turnaround for pressing needs
additional_notes: A program by a small US nonprofit to directly channel donations to field partners in need; minimal bureaucracy
